blocks.text: PAUL'S “PARTNER AND FELLOWHELPER” (2 CORINTHIANS 8:23) · CALLED IN GALATIANS 2: TAKEN TO JERUSALEM
Titus. A Greek believer, Paul's envoy to Corinth, left in Crete.
ALSO CALLED
No other name
FROM
Scripture does not say
TRADE
Scripture does not say
FAMILY
“Titus, who was with me, being a Greek”.
WRITINGS
The letter to Titus (addressed to him)
BACKGROUND
Home, trade and family
FAMILY
“Titus, who was with me, being a Greek”. Galatians 2:3
Paul calls him “mine own son after the common faith” and “Titus my brother”. Titus 1:4 2 Corinthians 2:13
THE CALLING
Called, as 2 accounts tell it
“Then fourteen years after I went up again to Jerusalem with Barnabas, and took Titus with me also.”
Galatians 2:1 (KJV) →
WHERE HE WENT
Acts and after
Jerusalem · Went up with Paul and Barnabas. Galatians 2:1
Troas · Paul looked for him here and did not find him. 2 Corinthians 2:12–13
Macedonia · Met Paul here with news from Corinth. 2 Corinthians 7:5–6
Corinth · Paul's envoy here. 2 Corinthians 7:13–15 2 Corinthians 8:6 +2 more
Crete · Left here to appoint elders. Called the bishop of its churches by Eusebius, about 325 (tradition). Titus 1:5
Nicopolis · Asked to join Paul here for the winter. Titus 3:12
Dalmatia · The last place Scripture names for him. 2 Timothy 4:10
Gortyna, in Crete · tradition · no map pin · Called its bishop in a late fragment ascribed to Zenas (tradition).
IN ACTS AND THE LETTERS

He went up to Jerusalem with Paul and Barnabas. Paul writes that Titus, “being a Greek”, was not “compelled to be circumcised”, and that to the “false brethren” who came in “we gave place by subjection, no, not for an hour”. Galatians 2:1–5
When Paul came to Troas he “had no rest in my spirit, because I found not Titus my brother”, and went on into Macedonia. 2 Corinthians 2:12–13

In Macedonia “God … comforted us by the coming of Titus”, who brought word of the Corinthians' “earnest desire”, “mourning” and “fervent mind”; his spirit “was refreshed by you all”. 2 Corinthians 7:5–7 2 Corinthians 7:13–15
Paul sent him to Corinth to finish the collection, with “the brother, whose praise is in the gospel throughout all the churches” and another brother. 2 Corinthians 8:6 2 Corinthians 8:16–24
“Did Titus make a gain of you? walked we not in the same spirit?” 2 Corinthians 12:17–18
The letter to him says: “For this cause left I thee in Crete, that thou shouldest set in order the things that are wanting, and ordain elders in every city”. Titus 1:5
Paul asks him, when Artemas or Tychicus comes, to come to Nicopolis for the winter, and to send Zenas the lawyer and Apollos on their way. Titus 3:12–13
2 Timothy says he had gone “unto Dalmatia”. 2 Timothy 4:10
COMPANIONS
Who was with him
Each line joins him to someone Scripture places beside him.
Paul Took him to Jerusalem, sent him to Corinth, left him in Crete; “my partner and fellowhelper”. Galatians 2:1 2 Corinthians 8:23 Titus 1:5
Barnabas Went up to Jerusalem with Paul and Titus. Galatians 2:1
Artemas Paul planned to send him or Tychicus to Titus, who was then to come to Paul at Nicopolis. Titus 3:12
Tychicus The other man Paul might send to Crete. Titus 3:12
Zenas “Zenas the lawyer”, to be sent on his way by Titus. Titus 3:13
Apollos To be sent on his way by Titus, “that nothing be wanting unto them”. Titus 3:13
Crescens and Demas Named beside him in 2 Timothy: Demas gone to Thessalonica, Crescens to Galatia, Titus to Dalmatia. 2 Timothy 4:10
HOW THE STORY ENDS
Scripture says, tradition says
SCRIPTURE SAYS
The last we read of him: “Titus unto Dalmatia” (2 Timothy 4:10). Scripture does not say whether he reached Paul at Nicopolis, or how he died. 2 Timothy 4:10 Titus 3:12
TRADITION SAYS
Eusebius writes that, “so it is recorded”, Timothy was first bishop at Ephesus and “Titus of the churches in Crete”.[1] Who says so: Eusebius, Church History 3.4.6, about AD 325

The Apostolic Constitutions list “Of Crete, Titus” among bishops ordained in the apostles' lifetime.[7] Who says so: Constitutions of the Holy Apostles 7.46, a compilation its ANF editor places “not later than the fourth century”

A fragment on the life of Titus ascribed to “the lawyer Zenas” makes him bishop of Gortyna in Crete and of a royal Cretan family; McGiffert calls the tradition “late, and, of course, of little authority”, though it “accords very well with all that we know of Titus”.[2][20] Who says so: a fragment “de Vita et Actis Titi”, as reported by McGiffert and Smith, late; date not given

Candia in Crete claims to be his burial place (McGiffert, citing Cave, 1677); Smith adds that he is “said to have been permanent bishop in the island, and to have died there at an advanced age”.[2][20] Who says so: local tradition, reported by Cave (1677), McGiffert and Smith, Cave, 1677, as reported by McGiffert (1890)
WRITINGS
Writings tied to him
LETTERS
The letter to Titus (addressed to him)
OPEN QUESTIONS
Where readers have differed
No: Paul did not yield
Lightfoot (1890), with “the vast majority of early writers”; Rutherfurd, ISBE (1915)
Lightfoot: the incident is told to show Paul never conceded circumcision, and Paul “could scarcely say ‘we yielded no not for an hour’ in the same breath” as confessing it. Galatians 2:3–5 [11][24]
Yes: he was circumcised, but not by compulsion
Farrar (1879); Pelagius, the one early exception Lightfoot found; “several modern critics” (Lightfoot)
Farrar asks why Paul's sentence is “so ambiguous, so involved” if he did not yield, and reads “was compelled” to mean Titus was circumcised “but not under compulsion”. Galatians 2:3 [12][11]
IN SCRIPTURE
Every passage
CHAPTERS · 8
Galatians 2 2 Corinthians 2 2 Corinthians 7 2 Corinthians 8 2 Corinthians 12 Titus 1 Titus 3 2 Timothy 4
PASSAGES · 9
Galatians 2:1–5 2 Corinthians 2:12–13 2 Corinthians 7:5–16 2 Corinthians 8:6 2 Corinthians 8:16–24 2 Corinthians 12:17–18 Titus 1:1–5 Titus 3:12–15 2 Timothy 4:10
WHAT SCRIPTURE DOES NOT SAY
Scripture does not name Titus's family or home town.
Scripture does not say when Paul and Titus were in Crete together, or whether Titus came to Nicopolis.
Scripture does not say why Titus went to Dalmatia, or what became of him.
Scripture does not call Titus a bishop.
IDENTIFICATIONS THIS PAGE RELIES ON

From the textActs never names Titus. Everything Scripture says of him is in Galatians, 2 Corinthians, 2 Timothy and the letter addressed to him. Galatians 2:1–3 2 Corinthians 2:13 2 Timothy 4:10 Titus 1:4
Scholars' viewSmith (1884) and Rutherfurd (ISBE, 1915) take “mine own son after the common faith” to mean that Paul brought him to faith. Titus 1:4 [20][24]

Scholars' viewSmith (1884) mentions that the “Titus Justus” of Acts 18:7 in the Revised Version is “possibly the same”; the KJV there reads only “Justus”. Kerr (ISBE, 1915) calls a suggested identification of Titus with Silas “very improbable”. This page relies on neither. Acts 18:7 [20][21]
